subject: Clarifying data-retention options for model inputs + evidence request
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Privacy Team <privacy@medtech.io>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@legalpartners.com>
Date: 2027-02-19T14:05:00-05:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — data handling options

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can evaluate internally: 

1) Our primary ask: can Redwood support a 0-retention mode for PII-containing prompts coming from our clinician-facing tools? We understand this has implications for caching and KV stores.
2) If 0-retention isn't feasible across the board, would Redwood commit to a hardened short-window (<=7 days) retention for specified routes and provide evidence of deletion?
3) We also need to confirm residency — all requests from EU clinicians must be processed in eu-west-1.

What would help our SOC/privacy review is:
- A short one-page statement on how Redwood enforces per-route retention policies (operational process + who has access).
- A sample audit log extract showing that a message was deleted/completed (redacted example ok).
- Confirmation whether model outputs are ever stored outside the configured retention window (beyond KV caching), and if so under what circumstances.

Can you and legal/engineering weigh in and we can lock a Mutual Action Plan for the PO?

Best,
Samantha
Director of Product, MedTech Co

----

Note: we are on a tight timeline for our pilot (contract by end of March).
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-19T16:22:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — data handling options

Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Appreciate the timeline. Below is a concrete breakdown of options and what we can provide as evidence. I am looping Marissa (Account Lead) and Karthik (Privacy/Product) to confirm implementation details.

Summary of options (short):
- Option A — Zero-retention for route: Redwood can be configured (per-route) to never persist request payloads beyond in-memory KV cache used for the in-flight request. No logs, no message bodies written to disk.
  - Tradeoffs: no post-hoc auditability for that raw input stream; limited model debugging unless your team ships deterministic prompt telemetry to a sandbox.
  - Evidence we can provide: redacted runtime log showing request processed and immediate deletion event, and a signed statement of our operational process.

- Option B — Short-window retention (configurable 1–14 days): full request metadata + body retained for N days, then purged.
  - Tradeoffs: gives you short-term debugging and quality monitoring; still bounded exposure.
  - Evidence: retention purge job run logs + sample audit extract after purge.

- Option C — Standard retention (30–90 days) with residency and audit controls: for customers who need traceability and QA.

Residency: we support per-tenant region pinning; routing to eu-west-1 is standard and we will ensure storage and processing are region-scoped for EU-labeled tenants.

Next steps I propose (mutual action plan draft):
1) MedTech confirms which routes need 0-retention vs short-window by 2027-02-25.
2) Redwood provides:
   - One-page process statement (operational controls) — 48 hours after confirmation.
   - Redacted sample audit extract demonstrating purge event — within 5 business days.
   - SOC2 summary and contact for compliance — attached.
3) Legal teams exchange a short addendum for the pilot defining retention windows and acceptance criteria — target 2027-03-08.

I've attached a proposed-retention-matrix.xlsx to help map routes.

Let me know if that timeline works and whether you want an EU-only pilot tenant.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@legalpartners.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
Cc: Privacy Team <privacy@medtech.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-20T09:48:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — data handling options

Thanks Grace — a few items from legal to clarify so we can scope the addendum: 

1) For Option A (0-retention), what is Redwood's definition of "no logs"? Specifically, do any ephemeral metrics or hashed identifiers persist outside of transient memory in a way that could be reconstructed?
2) For Option B, can Redwood provide a sample retention purge record (timestamped) showing deletion of a test message and the SHA256 hash (or similar) that proves the deletion correlated to a known object id? Redacted content is fine.
3) If region pinning is used, please confirm whether any configuration, deployment, or control-plane metadata is ever stored in a global system that would contain tenant identifiers. We need to know if any metadata could be visible to engineers in non-EU regions.

If Redwood can provide the one-page statement + one redacted purge record, we can draft the pilot addendum quickly.

Alex Rivera
Counsel, LegalPartners (external counsel for MedTech Co)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@legalpartners.com>, Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-02-22T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — data handling options

Alex — thanks. Quick answers and delivery plan below. 

Short answers: 
- "No logs" for Option A: means we do not persist request bodies or associated PII to disk or long-term logging systems. We do emit ephemeral metrics (e.g., request count, latency) that are aggregated and non-reconstructable; we do not persist unhashed identifiers.
- We can generate a timestamped purge record for Option B that includes a non-reversible digest (SHA256 of an internal object id) and purge job metadata; content will be redacted.
- Control plane metadata: tenant configuration (tenant id, routing policy) exists in our control plane; for EU-pinned tenants we mark residency flag and control plane access is limited to authorized roles. No raw PII is kept there; deployment artifacts do not contain message content.

Delivery plan: 
- By 2027-02-23 EOD: one-page operational process statement and SOC2 summary (attached).
- By 2027-02-26: redacted sample purge record and an example runtime log showing in-memory handling and delete event.
- Marissa will set up a sandbox EU tenant if you confirm EU-only pilot.

Proposed short action items: 
- MedTech: confirm pilot routes + residency requirement (reply by 2027-02-25).
- Redwood: deliver the artifacts above on the dates listed.

If that works I'll add these items into the shared Mutual Action Plan link: https://app.redwood.com/deals/MT-2027-0421/mutual-action-plan

Thanks — Grace
